grades: Ages 8 to 18 (Senior Project Achievement is grades 9 to 12)
name: Georgia 4-H
city: Georgia (county Extension offices statewide; state office in Athens, GA)
what_you_do: Join clubs, camps and projects in farming, science, civics, leadership and health. Older teens can join Project Achievement contests. They can join state conferences and leadership programs.
who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18. Cloverbud programs for ages 5 to 7 exist in some counties only.
pay_detail: Not a job. The page says 4-H does not require a uniform or club fees. Camps and some activities may have their own costs, not listed on this page.
duration: Ongoing; clubs, projects, camps and conferences run through the year
deadline_text: No enrollment dates listed. Ask your county Extension office.
how_to_apply: Contact your local county UGA Extension office, or Georgia 4-H at 706-542-4444 or ga4h@uga.edu. The site has a 'Find Your Local Club' page.
notes: The home page lists teen options. They are Ambassador Program, Leadership in Action, Step Up and Lead, Senior Conference, State Council and State Congress. The pages read did not give dates or ages for each. Check with the county office.
